documents.title: Quit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: hey doc, figured you'd want to know. I stopped smoking 2 weeks ago. Cold turkey, no patches. Guys on the crew still smoke so it's hard at lunch but so far so good

documents.title: RE: Quit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Henry, that's great news, the best thing you could do for your health. The first month is the hardest. If cravings get bad, patches or gum are fine to add, just tell me. Let's do a quick video check in June.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, he's in his truck after work, verified DOB.

No cigarettes since about 4/25, roughly seven weeks. Chewing a lot of sunflower seeds. Irritable the first ten days, better now. Not vaping. Mood fine, PHQ-9 4. Still on sertraline 50 daily.

A/P: Former smoker now. Problem list updated. Congratulated him. Not a candidate for lung screening at his age. Physical in October.

documents.title: Sertraline Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Sertraline 50 mg #90 request. Last visit 6/12. Approved per protocol, 1 refill, PCP to cosign.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
29 y/o M, yearly exam.

Interval: Still off cigarettes since April, proud of it. Put on a couple of pounds. Mood steady, PHQ-9 3, sertraline 50 daily. No joint pain or swelling ever. His dad had another bad gout flare this summer and Henry is worried he's next.

Labs from 10/9 reviewed: CMP normal, creatinine normal. CBC normal. Lipids fine. Uric acid 9.5, up again (8.4 in 2022, 8.9 last year).

Exam: Vitals as charted. Well. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Feet and hands: no swelling, no tophi. Skin normal. Mood/affect normal.

A/P:
1. Hyperuricemia, rising, no gout. Long talk. He wants to treat it given his father. Starting allopurinol 300 mg daily. Reviewed: stop and call for rash, fever, or any swelling. Recheck uric acid and kidney function in 2-3 months.
2. Depression: stable, continue sertraline.
3. Former smoker: keep it up.
4. Flu shot given today. He declined the COVID booster this year.

RTC 3 months.

orders.reason: acute kidney injury, suspected allopurinol interstitial nephritis

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Same-Day Visit: Leg Swelling
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Texted this morning, ankles puffy since the weekend and he's been wiped out at work, dragging by noon. Socks leave deep marks. Started allopurinol 300 on 10/16, so about two weeks in; has taken it daily. No rash, no fever, no burning or urgency with urination, no flank or back pain. No new NSAIDs or supplements. No chest pain or shortness of breath.

O: Vitals normal, as charted. Looks tired, not ill. No rash anywhere. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no CVA tenderness. Bilateral pitting edema of the lower legs. No joint swelling.

Labs (drawn today, back this afternoon): creatinine 2.3 (normal on 10/9), BUN 34. UA: protein 1+, blood 1+, RBC 8/hpf, WBC 2/hpf; no RBC casts and no bacteria on micro; nitrite and leukocyte esterase negative. Urine culture pending.

A/P:
1. Acute kidney injury two weeks after starting allopurinol, with edema, mild proteinuria and microscopic hematuria, bland for infection. Most likely drug-induced acute interstitial nephritis. Allopurinol stopped today. Called him at 3 pm with the numbers and told him to take no more.
2. Culture sent to be complete. Renal ultrasound this week. Repeat BMP in 1 week. Nephrology referral, asked for a prompt slot.
3. Avoid ibuprofen/naproxen, keep drinking water. Light duty if he can get it; work note given.
4. Return precautions: less urine, shortness of breath, worse swelling, fever, rash: call same day.
5. Allopurinol not to be restarted.

documents.title: Result Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP, called pt: urine culture no growth, no infection. Ankles a bit less puffy, still tired. Urinating normally. Off allopurinol since Thursday. Confirmed US tomorrow 2:30 and labs Thursday. He knows to call with any decrease in urine or new swelling.

reports.text:
INDICATION: Acute kidney injury.
TECHNIQUE: Grayscale and color flow sonography of both kidneys and the bladder.
FINDINGS: Right kidney 11.4 cm, left kidney 11.7 cm in length. Normal cortical thickness and echogenicity. No hydronephrosis. No calculi. No solid or cystic mass. Normal color flow. Bladder decompressed, unremarkable.

documents.title: BMP Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine down to 1.7 from 2.3, BUN 25. Ultrasound normal. Moving the right way off allopurinol. Message sent to pt. Nephrology on the 20th.

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEPHROLOGY GROUP, consultation letter
Visit 11/20/2024. Reason: acute kidney injury.

Dear colleague, thank you for asking me to see Mr. Silva, 29, a construction worker with depression on sertraline and hyperuricemia.

He started allopurinol 300 mg daily on 10/16. Two weeks later he developed bilateral leg edema and fatigue, and your labs showed creatinine 2.3 from a normal baseline, BUN 34, and a urinalysis with mild proteinuria and microscopic hematuria without casts, pyuria or bacteria. Culture negative. Renal ultrasound normal. Allopurinol was stopped 10/31 and creatinine was 1.7 a week later.

Today he feels close to normal. Edema nearly gone. No rash, fever or joint pain.
Meds: sertraline 50 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: BP normal. No rash. Trace ankle edema. Otherwise unremarkable.
Labs today: creatinine 1.3.

Impression: Acute interstitial nephritis, most likely allopurinol-induced, recovering after withdrawal of the drug. With steady improvement I would not biopsy and would not give steroids.

Recommendations: avoid allopurinol permanently. Avoid NSAIDs while recovering. Repeat creatinine in 3 weeks; I expect it to normalize. If his uric acid needs treatment in future it should be discussed with us first. No routine nephrology follow-up needed unless creatinine fails to return to baseline.

Sincerely, consulting nephrologist

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: Kidney Injury
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Swelling gone for about two weeks. Energy back, working full days again since mid-November. No rash. Has stayed off allopurinol and off ibuprofen. Saw nephrology 11/20, letter reviewed: allopurinol-related interstitial nephritis, no biopsy, avoid allopurinol.

O: Vitals as charted. No edema. Heart and lungs normal.
BMP drawn just before the visit: creatinine 1.0, BUN 15. Back to his baseline.

A/P:
1. AKI / acute interstitial nephritis from allopurinol: resolved. Allopurinol is off his list for good; told him to say so at any pharmacy or ER.
2. Hyperuricemia: no gout. Leaving it untreated for now.
3. Depression: fine, PHQ-9 3.

Physical next fall.
